question: How many confirmed U.S. measles cases for 2026 will CDC report in its November 27, 2026 update?

calls.reasoning: Base: 5,412 as of Nov 12 (Nov 13 update). Recent increments +330, +230; October averaged ~240/wk (3,886 Oct 1 -> 4,852 Oct 29). Signs of slowing: outbreak-associated cases +223 last week, no new outbreaks added, Pennsylvania only +56 between Nov 9 and Nov 16. Two increments (~210 and ~180-220, holiday week possibly smaller) put the median near 5,830-5,850. Right skew: if no update appears on Nov 27, the first update after Nov 26 (likely ~Dec 4) governs, adding a third increment. Market check: the only candidate, Manifold's 'more cases in 2027 than 2026', has a different contract and is not an anchor; no Polymarket/Kalshi market on the CDC Nov 27 figure was found.
calls.dossier:
- CDC Measles page (fetched 2026-11-17): 5,412 confirmed 2026 cases as of Nov 12 (Nov 13 update); data cutoff is 12:00 PM ET Thursday, published Fridays.
- CDC weekly totals (question background): 3,294 (Sep 10), 3,659 (Sep 24), 3,886 (Oct 1), 4,852 (Oct 29), 5,182 (Nov 5, +330), 5,412 (Nov 12, +230). Oct 1->Oct 29 averages ~240/wk.
- ContagionLive, Nov 13 2026: +4.4% week over week (+230) after +6.8% (+330); 43 outbreaks with none added this week; outbreak-associated cases +223 (4,993 -> 5,216); 47 jurisdictions.
- PA DOH via US News, Nov 16 2026: PA 1,561 cases in 46 counties (1,505 on Nov 9, so +56 in a week; +19 since Nov 13); 309 hospitalizations, 7 deaths in state data.
- US News, Nov 16 2026: US declared to have lost measles elimination status (Nov 13).
- 2025 precedent (CIDRAP): early Dec 2025 update showed 1,912 (+84 week over week) around Thanksgiving week; CDC appears to have kept a weekly cadence through the holiday in 2025 (then on Wednesdays).
- Resolution: resolves off the CDC national 2026 total in the update published Fri Nov 27, 2026. If none is published Nov 27, the first update published after Nov 26 governs; a Wed Nov 25 publication would NOT count, so the next one (~Dec 4, a third increment) would apply. Not JHU, PAHO, or state figures.
- Event window: single reading of the update published 2026-11-27 (or the first after Nov 26). As of Nov 17, two weekly updates remain (~Nov 20 and ~Nov 27).
- Upward drivers: 13+ consecutive triple-digit weeks; holiday travel; low-coverage states (e.g. Idaho ~75% kindergarten MMR); clusters in SC (~670), WI, MN.
- Downward drivers: PA slowing; no new outbreaks added; Thanksgiving reporting lag could shrink the holiday-week increment or shift the cutoff earlier.
- Searched but not found: CDC statement on Thanksgiving-week publication timing; Nov 20 figure (not yet published); a human prediction market on this exact figure.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs share the same CDC series and slowing signals (PA ~+56/wk, no new outbreaks, SC/UT at zero for 4 weeks). They differ mainly on the chance that the governing update is the ~Dec 4 one, which adds a third increase. That depends on CDC's Thanksgiving schedule, which no run found and which I cannot check without web access. I weighted ~45% Fri Nov 27, ~30% early or skipped (which pushes resolution to ~Dec 4), and ~25% late Mon/Tue (still about two increases). That puts the 3-increase scenario at ~30%, below Run 2's ~50%, so my median lands near Runs 1 and 3. I keep a dispersion of ~400, similar to Run 3's. Neither open bound has a realistic escape mechanism.
